items.why: Short answer with have got: Yes, I have.

items.q: We ___ two maps in the bag.

items.a: My sister has got two phones

items.s: It’s raining — have you got an ___? ☂️
I can’t open the door. Where are my ___? 🔑
I don’t know this city. Have you got a ___? 🗺
“What time is it?” — “I haven’t got a ___.” ⌚
My laptop and my books are in my ___. 👜

lines: This is my bag. [I’ve got|I have|I has got] a laptop and two books in it.
[There’s|There are|It’s] an umbrella, too, because it’s raining.
My sister [has got|have got|has get] a bigger bag, but she [hasn’t got|haven’t got|doesn’t got] a laptop.
“[Have|Has|Do] you got a map?” — “No, [I haven’t|I’ve not|I don’t].”
We [haven’t got|hasn’t got|not have got] a car, but we’ve got two [bicycles|bicycle|a bicycles].

tts: 70% of people in the world have got a mobile phone.
9% of people in the world have got a car.
20% of people in the world have got a TV.
30% of people in the world have got a bank account.
2% of people in the world have got a pet.
40% of people in the world have got a bicycle.

acts.title: Nine cats
text: My name’s Dana. I haven’t got a pet. 🚫🐱
But my mother has got nine cats! 🐱
She hasn’t got a big house — it’s small, but it’s got a garden. 🌳
In my family we haven’t got cars. I haven’t got a car,
my brother hasn’t got a car — but we’ve all got bicycles. 🚲

items.s: Dana’s mother has got nine cats.
Her mother’s house has got a garden.
Dana’s brother has got a car.

items.sit: It is raining. You want to know if your colleague has an umbrella.
Someone asks: “Have you got a laptop?” You have one.
Someone asks: “Has your family got a car?” You have not.
You cannot find your keys and you ask your partner.
o: Do you have got my keys?

items.sit: You talk about your sister. She owns two phones.
A colleague asks what is in your bag.
o: I’ve got a laptop and two books.
I have got laptop and two book.

write.q: Write 5 sentences: three things you have got, one thing you haven’t got, and one thing someone in your family has got.
write.model: I’ve got a phone, a laptop and a wallet in my bag. I’ve got two keys. I haven’t got a car. My sister has got a bicycle. My parents haven’t got a pet.

speak.q: Say what is in your bag right now. Then ask two “Have you got…?” questions out loud.
speak.model: I’ve got a phone, a wallet and an umbrella in my bag. Have you got a map? Have you got a pen?
